explanations: There is no defect. Prices are looked up server-side from the menu and never read from the request; unknown fields are rejected by extra="forbid"; quantities and tips use strict ints so strings or floats are not coerced; the pattern fields are anchored with ^ and $; item and note sizes are bounded; the scheduled time must be timezone-aware before it is compared with an aware "now", avoiding a naive/aware TypeError; and the cross-field rules live in a model_validator so they run only after every field is individually valid. Duplicate item ids are rejected before the price lookup so a quantity cap cannot be bypassed by splitting a line.

The "asap" branch of check_schedule raises ValueError if scheduled_for is set; FastAPI turns the resulting validation error into a 422 before the route body (and thus the restaurant lookup) runs. It is not ignored (A), no 409 is involved (C), and the type is never switched (D).

The model has no uniqueness rule; the route checks len(set(ids)) != len(ids) after confirming the restaurant exists and is open, returning a 422. The per-line limit alone would allow it (A), merging never happens (D), and the model-level validators do not look for duplicates (B).

quantity is declared with strict=True, which disables the usual str-to-int coercion, so validation fails and FastAPI answers 422. Without strict mode A would be true. The JSON is well formed (C) and the lookup is never reached (D).
